card.name: Degree adverbs like fully and absolutely
card.fires_on: Intensifier or degree words such as fully, absolutely, completely, utterly and unsure, placed just before an adjective or verb in general web prose. Often follows a negation or modal like not, may not or don't.

modes.label: Fully after negation
modes.description: A degree adverb right after not or never, before a verb of understanding.
modes.example: even he may not<< fully>> understand.

modes.label: Absolutely as emphasis
modes.description: An intensifier before an adjective in enthusiastic or emphatic writing.

modes.label: Split adverb endings
modes.description: The ending of a split intensifier such as absolutely or utterly.
modes.example: WE ONLY PRINT MATERIAL WHEN ABSOLUT<<ELY>> NECESSARY

card.plain: It fires on emphasis words like fully, absolutely and completely just before the word they strengthen.
evidence: even he may not<< fully>> understand.
